video_title: Boogie, Lou & Chandler SHOCKED After Knicks Comeback Win!

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Michelle Beadle calls Cavaliers' Game 1 loss a choke and collapse
quotes.excerpt: Have you ever seen something this atrocious in a playoff game?
quotes.quote: Largest playoff comeback in franchise history. That's not what you want for a playoff game, guys. 93-71 is where we were with 7:52 left in the game and they end up losing by 11 points. I was once told by Lawrence Frank to never use the word choke or collapse. I'm going to use both of those right now. Have you ever seen something this atrocious in a playoff game?

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons criticizes Kenny Atkinson's scared coaching decisions
quotes.excerpt: Kenny Atkinson allowing a 23-4 run without calling one timeout when he had two timeouts left.
quotes.quote: Kenny Atkinson allowing a 23-4 run without calling one timeout when he had two timeouts left. Going to Hack-a-Robinson with seven and a half minutes to me when they were up 22 points just showed me that this was a scared basketball team. They started bogging the game down, they started going deep into the shot clock, slowing it down. There's one play they had a three-on-one fast break and they literally pulled it out because they wanted to milk the clock and that just sent the wrong message with seven, eight minutes left in this game.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons questions Cavaliers' player performance and defensive substitutions
quotes.excerpt: Why did it take so long to get James Harden out of there when he wasn't really going nuts offensively?
quotes.quote: Jalen Brunson was sublime in this fourth quarter, he hit so many tough shots. But this is what he does. Why did it take so long to double team him to get the ball out of his hands? Why did it take so long to get James Harden out of there when he wasn't really going nuts offensively? And Max Strus, who's been doing a great job defensively all playoffs long, is sitting on the bench. Sam Merrill was on the bench that started. Mobley was on the bench that started, he'd be one of the best defensive players, he'd win Defensive Player of the Year. And then we have Schroder and Keon Ellis on the bench who are fantastic on-ball defenders. And you're allowing them to put James Harden in situations where he struggles and he got cooked when it mattered the most. And again, he had a big pull-up there at the end, but that's really all he contributed down the stretch. So this was a combination of just I think bad coaching and just bad executing, bad substitutions, just a real combination of everything bad that happened for Cleveland and Jalen Brunson exposed them. He found the open man when they did start doubling him and he made an insane run there in the fourth quarter.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams blames Cavaliers' collapse on coaching and James Harden's defense
quotes.excerpt: It was a total collapse from the Cleveland Cavaliers. But it started with James Harden and it ended with Kenny Atkinson.
quotes.quote: But every once in a while you got to call a spade a spade. You don't even know where to place blame in this. It was so many opportunities for the Cleveland Cavaliers to make adjustments to stop this from happening. Nothing was adjusted from the coaching to James Harden to having Schroder on the bench. I understand he's one for nine from the field, but that's not what you ask Dennis Schroder to do anyway. You ask him to junk up the game, guard your best players and give you an opportunity to get stops. In a collapse like that where you got a guy like James Harden in 19 straight switches that a team is seeking him out, you put somebody else on the floor that can kind of patch that up for you. So that's on Kenny Atkinson. Also, like Chandler just said, you have two timeouts that you can go to to go to those adjustments to put other people in the game to give you an opportunity. Didn't do that as well. James Harden didn't take the challenge as well. We can talk about all of these other guys, but when a team is seeking you out, you got to sit down. El Frank said that to you, I also had a coach tell me, it's no help when somebody is straight line driving you. If somebody is going straight down the gut of your defense, we can't even help you with that. That's something that you got to be able to keep the ball in front of you. So time and time again last night from the fourth quarter to the overtime, it was a total collapse from the Cleveland Cavaliers. But it started with James Harden and it ended with Kenny Atkinson.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins believes Cavaliers should have pulled James Harden
quotes.excerpt: I thought the best decision for the Cavaliers to try to close that game out was to pull James Harden.
quotes.quote: I agree. To piggyback off Lou, it started with James Harden and it ended with Kenny Atkinson. It was to a point where I thought the best decision for the Cavaliers to try to close that game out was to pull James Harden. I think anybody in that situation would have been better, especially with the performance down the stretch. Like you said, he wasn't having the greatest offensive night. The urgency wasn't there, the poise wasn't there, the leadership wasn't there. So I think at that point in the game, anybody would have been the better option to even avoid getting to that overtime situation. And that goes back to coaching as well. That's a tough decision to make in the moment, in a conference finals game, to pull one of your best players, but those type of decisions do fall on coaching and I think Atkinson should have made the ultimate decision.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel discusses Cavaliers' defensive struggles and passive strategy against Knicks
quotes.excerpt: He wasn't giving what he usually does offensively, so why am I allowing them to go on this 23-4 run?

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: James Harden should have pulled himself after so many of those.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: The problem is we're used to this from James Harden on the defensive end, but sometimes, and most of the time, he's so good offensively that you live with this and you deal with this. Last night he was one for eight from the three-point line, he had six turnovers, and he was five for 16 from the field. He wasn't giving what he usually does offensively, so why am I allowing them to go on this 23-4 run while I leave him in the game when again, like Lou said, we got guys like Schroder who are there to annoy Jalen Brunson and to pick him up 94 feet. Keon Ellis is the same type of guy. Max Strus just did the same thing to Cade Cunningham and he's on the bench while we need stops.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: What do you think that is? I don't want to play psychologist here, but why do you think that is? Because I think it ends up the math is like a 44-11 run in fourth quarter and overtime.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: 44-11 in fourth quarter and overtime.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: I think they're just thinking at that point if even if we just trade baskets, we're okay. We got a 15-point lead, we got a 17-point lead. But then once they started bogging the game down, they started to just milking the clock. Then they stopped doing what got them the lead and then they were just giving up points.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: They were playing keep away. They weren't playing to win. They were trying not to lose the basketball.

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: They were playing not to lose.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams questions Cavaliers' coaching loyalty and lack of adjustments
quotes.excerpt: You also got to read the room and know the game and say, hey look, this is not personal.
quotes.quote: It can be a loyalty thing. And at the end of the day, that's one of your top two best players on the floor. So yes, you have a certain responsibility to keep him on the floor, especially if you're going to need scoring when a team is making a run. But you also got to read the room and know the game and say, hey look, this is not personal, I got to give us an opportunity to get out of here and steal this Game 1 in Madison Square Garden, especially with the way that we played for three and a half quarters. This was a game for us to win. This was a great opportunity for us to start this series off before this team got going. It felt like in the fourth quarter, New York finally woke up. They probably were a little rusty and they started playing the basketball that got them to this position. And Cleveland just didn't respond well from it, from the players not playing with any pace, not playing with any aggression after getting a big lead, to Kenny Atkinson not making any adjustments. It just was a total meltdown from top to bottom.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel discusses Knicks' resilience and Cavaliers' failure to defend Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: They allowed Jalen Brunson to play in, he's the best ISO player in the game.

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: I just don't understand, you know how the Knicks are built, you know who the shots are going to and it's still nothing defensively, not even a trap, a soft trap across half court.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: What have we seen all playoffs long?

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: Just take the ball out of his hands.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Thank you, Boogie. We've watched all playoffs long, we've watched teams take the ball out of the best player's hands before he crosses half court. We're going to let somebody else do it. You're not going to do it. They allowed Jalen Brunson to play in, he's the best ISO player in the game. You let him walk down, seek out the switch that he wanted and he played one-on-one for seven and a half minutes.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: And think about it, Clarkson, zero, three points. McBride, zero points. OG was one for six from the field. These are the type of guys that I would rather sleep well at night knowing that they beat me and made shots than Jalen Brunson who's been doing this for years. Clutch player of the year, down the stretch. Most fourth quarter points. That's the guy that you let go on a single-handedly individual 10-0 run against the same guy that's guarding him and no adjustments, no timeouts to even give the poor guy a break.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Also, why are we keeping timeouts for?

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel debates coaching decisions and the fear of outside opinions
quotes.excerpt: You can't coach worrying about what outside opinions feel about your decision making.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: You know what though, let's think about this. Let's say he did pull James Harden yesterday. And I don't even know what the ending matters. But if he would have pulled James Harden.

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: They probably win the game.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: They win the game.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: But would anybody be on him today?

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: If you pull James Harden and you win the basketball game, I don't care if he's upset.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: What if you pull him and you lose? Do we kind of manipulate this?

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: There's always that fear that okay, now if they go cold offensively then it's going to look bad with James on the bench. Kenny, that's a calculated risk. But what was happening defensively with him?

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: It's better than a 44-10 run.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: But you can't coach worrying about what outside opinions feel about your decision making. You can't coach that. You can't coach that way. So we can't get inside of his head and wonder what he was thinking, but there was a lot of decisions out there that lead us to believe that this was an opportunity for him to make adjustments and he didn't. So again, was it scared coaching? Was it I trust my guys? Was it loyalty? It feels like all of these things. Those are the questions that need to be answered after a collapse like this.
